rule_hypotheses.rule: Payout = min(Max Benefit, covered charges - credits). When covered in-term rent and damages exceed Max Benefit, approved = Max Benefit exactly.
When every billed item is a covered type (cleaning, repairs, painting, blinds, lawn, bulbs, in-term rent), approved = the PM statement's 'balance/amount due' exactly.

Explicit exclusions (post-mid-2023/2024 claims): SDRP/deposit-waiver premiums, RBP/resident-benefit/renters-insurance fees, late fees, paper-payment/admin fees are not paid; cleaning and unpaid in-term rent shortfalls are paid.
Pet damage is excluded (PM note on 502: 'No coverage for pet damages. Paying remaining eligible covered repairs').

Pre-program-era 2023 claims (approved before 12/1/2023) were paid at the PM ledger balance with little scrutiny: utilities (300 temp utilities), pet-fee forfeit and a 1-day holdover rent were all paid.

Credits are subtracted before paying: cash security deposit + refundable pet deposit applied (163), tenant prepaid credit balance (693), tenant partial payment/referral credit (349), third-party housing-authority payments (71).
Unpaid rent within the lease term is paid at the actual shortfall per month (billed rent minus partial payment), not a full month.
Adjuster pays what the PM actually billed the tenant (final statement), not the vendor estimate or owner-responsible items.
Decline (0) when the tenant's first full-month rent payment was returned/defaulted and/or when, after third-party payments, only excluded items (eviction legal, maintenance coordination fee) remain.

Rent-based cap (monthly rent rounded up to next $500) did not bind anywhere in this batch: never applied in 2022 (11 paid 3500 on rent 2175); for 2023-2024 claims payouts were below the rent cap or the rent cap equalled Max Benefit (812, 980, 502: rent 2100-2295 -> 2500 = Max).
2022 claims pay exactly Max Benefit when charges exceed it, including eviction-related claims.

extraction_lessons: Texas REALTORS TXR-2216 'Itemization of Security Deposit' (GDAA/PURE Austin, claims 11, 135, 980) is usually a SCAN with no text layer: read lines (1)-(19) visually; line (1) free text often lists sub-items with amounts ('rekey $85.52, haul off $541.25 ...'); the total owed is the parenthesised 'Balance of Security Deposit after Deductions'.

PURE 'Security Deposit Statement' / 'deposit_disposition_amount_due' letters list Credits and Charges and an 'Amount Due'; 'Charge Forward' lines have no description - reconcile them against the ledger by amount (rent remainder, late-charge remainder, posting fee, RBP/RCP).

PURE tenant ledgers (Rent Manager style) are chronological with running balance; a negative balance is a tenant credit that the adjuster subtracts (693). Move-out charges post as 'Deposit Forfeit - <item>'.

Propertyware ledgers (New Heights 71, StarPointe 163) are reverse-chronological with Paid/Unpaid/Partially Paid Charge statuses and huge payment-allocation text blocks; the header 'Total Unpaid' is the claim balance; 'SECDEP applied' credit memos = deposit applied.
A ledger can predate the final disposition and miss items (693: ledger 07/26 has 2 move-out charges, disposition 07/29 has 4) - prefer the latest-dated statement.
Vendor estimates can exceed what the PM billed (337: estimate 1365 vs statement 490); pay the statement.
Some folders lack any PM statement: 502 only has the waiver addendum; 349 only has tenant phone screenshots of an email dispute (PNG, vision needed) - amounts must be reconstructed from email text.
Duplicate files with '(1)'/'(2)' suffixes are byte-identical copies (11) - dedupe before summing.
zInspector move-out photo reports (135 '1307.pdf', 64 pages) carry the make-ready list/estimate only on the first 1-2 pages.

Sheet fields are unreliable: Monthly Rent may be wrong (349 sheet 1520 vs lease 1820; 693 sheet 1272 is the MTM rate vs lease 995), Posted Date can precede Claim Date (410), move-out dates conflict with docs (135). Use the lease/ledger for rent and term.

The workbook 'Comments' sheet 'Row N' keys do NOT line up with tracking-number rows (e.g. the Row 12 comment talks about a Sept 2024 lease end, but tracking 11 is a 2022 claim; Row 813 comment cites policy 647R that does not exist on tracking 812) - treat like the misaligned 'Amount of Claim' column.
Lease end date matters for rent coverage; the sheet often leaves it blank (11, 71, 135, 163) - pull Commencement/Expiration from the lease (TXR leases: 'Commencement Date ... Expiration Date ...').
